prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalledress", with the standing line "A desktop studio that turns a short seed phrase into a prompt, and then into an image, by drawing words from curated databases." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A typed seed phrase, "Person Tour Coordinates", enters at left and is pressed into a fixed key. The key moves into a tall wooden card catalogue whose drawers are word databases. A series stencil lies over the drawer fronts, so only permitted words can be pulled. Exactly one card rises from each open drawer. The cards gather on a tray into a single written prompt. An arrow carries the prompt right to an image provider. A second arrow brings the finished image back.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one shows the same seed giving the same key within a series. circle two shows the stencil letting only listed words through a drawer. circle three shows a cache hit, where stored artifacts are reused instead of generated again. study one shows a sealed built-in series beside an editable user series. study two shows the embedded archive unpacked into a cache and rebuilt when its hash changes. study three shows a colour-limit dial running from two-tone to seven-tone.

Colour is used so that Ochre marks the seed and its key. Teal marks the words that were picked and the prompt built from them. Vermilion marks the finished image artifacts.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 19 word databases drawn as drawers. 13 filter fields on each series stencil. 7 working phases along the foot. 6 image models listed beside the model selector.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: Seed, Series, Model, Background, Enhance prompt, Generate image, Annotate, Preview, Generate, adverbs, adjectives, nouns, emotions, occupations, actions, artstyles, litstyles, colors, viewpoints, gazes, backstyles, compositions, Built-in, user-series, series.tar.gz, Color limit, Generated, Annotated, Prompt, Metadata, Export Text, setup, base_prompts, enhance_prompt, image_prep, image_wait, image_download, annotate, gpt-image-2.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: Seed, Series, Background, nouns, adjectives, emotions, occupations, artstyles, viewpoints, backstyles, Enhance prompt, image provider stable seed, cache hit Built-in, user-series, series.tar.gz, Color limit Generated, Annotated, Prompt, Metadata, Export Text, gpt-image-2 setup, image_wait, annotate

Set these short notes beside what they explain: One record pulled from each database; Series decides which words are allowed. Same seed, new series, different image; Cached artifacts skip the provider entirely. Built-in series are read-only; User series shadow built-ins by name. Records reveal which row made each word. Preview builds the prompt without an image.
